topIssues.title: op-reth: delay proofs ExEx acknowledgements until indexing completes
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
## Description

The proofs-history ExEx can emit `FinishedHeight` immediately after scheduling asynchronous catch-up with `sync_to`, before the proof engine has indexed that height. This can let reth prune the replay data that catch-up still needs.

When catch-up reaches a block whose parent state is not available yet, `StateForHashNotFound` is currently converted to success without advancing the proof tip. The engine resets its retry backoff on that apparent success and can retry the same block in a tight loop.

## Expected behavior

- Emit `FinishedHeight` only for heights the proof engine has actually indexed.
- Treat unavailable parent state as a no-progress retry and apply exponential backoff.
- Resume and acknowledge progress once the state becomes available.

## Context

Found while reviewing the reth v2.6.0 bump: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/23046#discussion_r4135197920

topIssues.title: op-reth: include pending block logs in eth_getLogs ranges
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
`eth_getLogs` ranges whose upper bound is `pending` currently resolve that bound to the canonical head unless the range also starts at `pending`. Requests such as `latest..pending` therefore return successfully while omitting logs from the local pending block.

This is not flashblock-specific: op-reth omits sequencer flashblock logs, while upstream Reth omits logs from its locally built pending block when pending-block construction is enabled.

The focused fix is in draft PR #23103, stacked on the Reth update in #23046. Original review finding: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/23046#discussion_r4135197967

topPRs.title: Add Lean proof of the super-aggregation coverage checks
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
Adds a Lean proof that `SuperAggregationInputs::validate` only accepts aggregations whose child outputs form one contiguous chain of super roots from the starting root to the root claim, with one range-derived block per chain and one consolidation step at every timestamp in between.

The Rust is extracted with Charon and Aeneas into `rust/kona/sp1/verification`. The main theorem is `KonaSp1.aggregation_sound`. It assumes child-proof soundness and `l2_sequence_number < u64::MAX`; the README lists the full trust base. `#print axioms` shows only Lean's standard axioms and the opaque super-root hash.

The `super_root.rs` change is only to suit the extractor: loops that returned early from nested or post-`?` positions move into private helpers, with the same accepted inputs and error order. A new test covers a chain-ID mismatch in a later timestamp block, the one loop that was rewritten rather than moved.

CI does not build the Lean project yet. `scripts/extract.sh` regenerates the generated files and `lake build` checks the proofs.

topPRs.title: kona-sp1: accelerate EIP-2537 BLS12-381 precompiles
topPRs.author: wwared
topPRs.body:
The kona-sp1 guest ran the EIP-2537 precompiles (0x0b–0x11) on revm's software arkworks backend, so any block that used them was expensive to prove. `CustomCrypto` now runs all seven on `sp1_bls12_381`, which uses SP1's field, point and bigint syscalls. In SP1's executor that is 5–26× fewer cycles per op (pairing 9.4×, G1 MSM 7.2×, G2 MSM 6.2×). Cycle counts overstate the proving saving, since syscalls cost more trace area; the one op measured in prover gas, a single-term G1 MSM, costs 3.6× less.

There is no behaviour change for chains or operators. The new backend must match arkworks bit for bit, including which `PrecompileHalt` wins when an input is invalid in several ways, because any divergence would make the proof disagree with the chain.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/proofs-team/issues/11

**Pieces**
- `crates/client/src/precompiles/bls12_381.rs`: the backend. It decodes and encodes EIP-2537 bytes itself, because `sp1_bls12_381`'s serializers use ZCash flag bits. The module doc lists the APIs it must not use and the zkVM hint paths it relies on.
- `crates/bls12-381-check` (test-only): a vendored copy of revm's arkworks backend as the oracle, and a deterministic 1340-case corpus (torsion and off-subgroup points, non-canonical encodings, error precedence, MSM and pairing inputs at the Jovian and Isthmus caps). Host tests compare `CustomCrypto` with arkworks and blst and run the official EIP-2537 vectors.
- `programs/tests/bls12-381-check` (test-only guest) and `examples/zkvm_check.rs`: run the corpus through `CustomCrypto` and in-guest arkworks inside SP1's executor, the only place `sp1_bls12_381`'s syscall and hint paths run, and print per-op cycles (`just check-bls12-381-zkvm`).
- `.circleci/continue/rust-e2e.yml`: a nightly `sp1-bls12-381-zkvm-check` job that runs that check (executor only; proving the corpus nightly is too costly).

**Review focus**
- Error precedence: MSM stops at the first error and validates each point before dropping a zero-scalar term; pairing skips identity pairs by their raw bytes, as revm does.
- Malicious-prover guards: the `g2_to_affine` assert and the `read_fp` pre-check only fire on a forged hint, so no test exercises them. Re-audit the module doc's hint list whenever `sp1_bls12_381` changes.
- u = 0 in `map_fp2_to_g2`: `sp1_bls12_381`'s G2 map (inherited from zkcrypto `bls12_381`) returns an off-curve point there, so that input returns the reference output directly. Not reported upstream yet.
- The nightly job can't run on this PR; its first run is the first nightly on `develop`, and a failure pages @proofs-team.

**Design choices**
- MSMs with fewer than four terms use per-term multiplication, which is cheaper than the bucket method's fixed per-window cost. A G1-only affine point-syscall loop would cut 1–3-term G1 MSMs another 4.3× in prover gas; rejected as extra hand-written code for a rare op.
- The new job restores the toolchain cache twice to stay simple. The G1 map keeps its isogeny-kernel guard: the output is the same without it, but it keeps `clear_h` off a degenerate point.

topPRs.title: kona-sp1: check below-head interop messages against log commitments
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
Part 2 of 3. #23361 adds the log-commitment program, this PR checks messages against its proofs in the consolidation, and PR 3 makes the proposer request those proofs.

Today the SP1 consolidation loads every receipt of an initiating block to check one message. For a full 30M-gas block, that is about 72M PGU and 3.7 MB of witness per message, and any log in the expiry window is a valid target. This PR checks a message into a block below the initiating chain's local-safe head against the block's entry from the log-commitment program (#23361) and a Merkle opening. That costs about 0.1M PGU per message, plus an EIP-2935 step for far blocks.

Cannon keeps the receipts path. A block without an entry also keeps it, so the proposer works unchanged until PR 3 requests sub-proofs. The public values, the game, and the contracts do not change. The consolidation stdin gains item 2: deploy the host before or with the new ELF, because an old host with the new ELF halts.

Testing: every `graph.rs` case runs through both paths. The ELF matches native with and without entries. A CPU-proved batch proves a consolidation, and entries that differ from the batch proof do not prove. Replacement rounds are tested at the graph level only.

topPRs.title: op-chain-ops: add eth-liquidity-pause command
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #23348 (`karl/eth-liquidity-pause`). That PR makes `ETHLiquidity` mirror the chain's L1 pause through the permissionless `L1CrossDomainMessenger.syncETHLiquidityPause()`.

## What it's for

`op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause` is a small CLI for the ETHLiquidity pause. It has three uses:

- **Devnet gate `interop.eth-liquidity-pause`:** `devnet-pause` → `status --expect paused` → `devnet-unpause` → `status --expect unpaused`.
- **Production verification:** `status` is read-only and works on any chain. Production pausing stays with the guardian's existing DeputyPauseModule flow, and this tool never pauses production. Nothing new is needed in superchain-ops.
- **Mirroring an L1 pause (or unpause, or expiry) to L2:** `sync` is permissionless, so any funded key can run it.

## Commands

- **`status --l2 <rpc>... [--l1 <rpc> --l1-messenger <addr>...] [--expect paused|unpaused] [--json]`**
  - For each chain it reads `ETHLiquidity.paused()` and `pausedL1Timestamp()`.
  - It runs an `eth_call` of `SuperchainETHBridge.sendETH` with 1 wei. A state override funds the dummy `--from`, so the sender needs no balance. It reports whether the call reverts and with which error (selector and name).
  - With `--l1`, it also shows `L1CrossDomainMessenger.paused()`, which is the ETHLockbox pause, and prints `OUT OF SYNC` when L1 and L2 differ.
  - `--expect` exits non-zero on any mismatch. For `paused`, every chain needs `paused()` true, `sendETH` reverting with `ETHLiquidity_Paused()` and, if read, L1 paused.
- **`sync --l1 <rpc> --l2 <rpc> --l1-messenger <addr> ... --key <any funded key>`**
  - Checks that each messenger's `SystemConfig.l2ChainId()` matches the `--l2` it is paired with.
  - Prints the L1 and L2 state per chain and skips chains already in sync (`--force` overrides).
  - Calls `syncETHLiquidityPause()`, waits for the L1 receipt, then polls L2 until `paused()` equals the L1 pause at the sync's block, or `--timeout` passes.
- **`devnet-pause` / `devnet-unpause --guardian-key <key>`**
  - Resolves each chain's ETHLockbox identifier through messenger → SystemConfig → portal → lockbox. Chains that share a lockbox are handled once.
  - Checks that the key is the SuperchainConfig guardian.
  - Calls `pause`, `extend` (if an earlier pause expired) or `unpause` on the lockbox identifier, then runs `sync`.
  - `devnet-unpause` warns if a global pause is still active.
  - Refuses OP Mainnet, Ink, Unichain, their Sepolia chains (10, 57073, 130, 11155420, 763373, 1301) and an L1 of Ethereum mainnet. There is no override flag.

Every flag can also come from `--config <toml>` (see `config.example.toml`). Local `*.toml` files in that directory are gitignored because they may hold keys.

## Usage

```bash
# Production / any chain: read-only
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause status \
  --l2 https://mainnet.optimism.io --l2 <ink-rpc> --l2 <unichain-rpc> \
  --l1 <eth-rpc> --l1-messenger <op-l1cdm> --l1-messenger <ink-l1cdm> --l1-messenger <uni-l1cdm>

# Mirror the current L1 pause to L2 (permissionless)
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause sync --config pause.toml --key <funded-l1-key>

# Devnet gate
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause devnet-pause   --config devnet.toml
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause status         --config devnet.toml --expect paused
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause devnet-unpause --config devnet.toml
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause status         --config devnet.toml --expect unpaused
```

## Tests

None of these tests need a network.

- **Calldata:** encoding for `paused()`, `syncETHLiquidityPause()`, `sendETH`, and SuperchainConfig `pause`/`unpause`/`extend`/`pausable`/`paused(address)`.
- **ABI drift:** a test checks every hand-written signature and custom error against the contracts-bedrock ABI snapshots on this stack, so a rename in #23348 fails here.
- **Revert decoding:** custom errors and `Error(string)` reasons.
- **Safety checks:** production refusal, `--l2`/`--l1-messenger` pairing, grouping chains by shared lockbox, the guardian pause/extend/unpause choice, and `--expect` evaluation, including L1 paused while L2 is not synced.
- **Config loading:** TOML values load into each command, including the example config.
- **`status` end to end:** runs against in-process fake L1/L2 JSON-RPC servers. The cases are paused and synced, unpaused, out of sync, a pre-pause ETHLiquidity, a messenger paired with the wrong chain, and JSON output. The fake rejects `sendETH` without the balance override, as geth does.
- **`sync` end to end:** runs on geth simulated backends with mock contracts. The cases are skip when in sync, `--force` send and wait for L2, a reverting call never sent, and an L2 timeout.

```
go test ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause/...   # ok
go vet ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause/...    # clean
./linter/bin/op-golangci-lint run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause/...   # 0 issues
go mod tidy -diff                                    # clean
```

I also ran `status` read-only against OP Mainnet and OP Sepolia public RPCs. ETHLiquidity is not initialized there yet, and the tool reports `Error("Proxy: implementation not initialized")` for both reads.

**Not run:** `sync` and `devnet-*` against a live devnet with #23348 deployed. The guardian path (`devnet-pause`/`devnet-unpause`) has unit coverage only for its decision logic.
